C-COMPACT-WINDOWS-FIT.Name: Compact-window fit and keyboard integrity for Quick Settings, Settings navigation and sheets — implementation plan
C-COMPACT-WINDOWS-FIT.IntentSummary: Draft plan for the approved-scope compact-window fit wave (frontend-design findings F-002/F-003/F-005/F-006/F-007/F-010, wave 35), all code facts verified at their cited lines on the beta-gate-wave tree. (1) Quick Settings viewport binding (R-1): the panel src/renderer/src/components/titleBar/quickSettings/index.vue is today a position:absolute top:calc(100% + 6px) 428px column whose ONLY height bound is the body's max-height: 62vh (overflow hidden on the panel itself, no panel max-height), so at the editor window's 600x400 minimum (tauri.conf.json minWidth 600 / minHeight 400) the toolbar, body and Open Settings footer must fit under the title bar with no total-height cap — the footer row clips and the body can double-limit against the remaining viewport. The fix keeps the approved mock metrics verbatim (428px width, 12px radius, the settings shadow, row anatomy, palette, open/close semantics) and adds ONLY a viewport height binding to the panel (max-height: calc(100vh - 64px), the constant reserving the title-bar strip plus the 6px gap on all platforms — the macOS strip is 30px padding per the tabsBar C-51 rule, Win/Linux frameless cells are 46px), flex-shrink: 0 on the .quick-toolbar and the .quick-openall footer, and the body becomes the single scroll region (flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; the existing overflow-y: auto kept) with max-height: 62vh deleted; proof is the new compact geometry walker (viewport-pinned e2e per the settings-shell.spec.ts canon) asserting every descendant rect inside the window rect at 600x400 on all three tabs, and unchanged approved metrics at 640x620 and 1440x900. (2) Settings toolbar fit (R-2): src/renderer/src/prefComponents/tabsBar/index.vue renders seven .pref-tab buttons (tabsBar/config.js TABS: general, appearance, editor, markdown, export, advanced, experimental) — mac centred column tabs with min-width: 76px, underline row tabs with no shrink floor — inside the fixed non-resizable 640x620 Settings window (m_v1_compat.rs mt_open_setting_window); the settings-shell e2e overflow walker covers .pref-body * only and never the toolbar. The fix keeps both platform variants, the macOS drag-region attribute (:data-tauri-drag-region="isOsx ? '' : null") and tab routing byte-identical, and adds ONLY: min-width: 0 on the base .pref-tab (shrink allowance; the mac variant keeps its 76px floor — 7x76px + 24px padding + gaps always fit 640px, so the floor never itself overflows), and on .pref-tab-label overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis (a flex child, so blockified — labels ellipsize instead of pushing tabs past the window edge). Proof: the walker extension to .pref-toolbar, .pref-toolbar * in settings-shell.spec.ts (scrollWidth at most innerWidth, every .pref-tab rect inside the viewport) including a stress run seeded through the prefs shim with the longest-label shipped locale catalog — de (preferences.tabs.appearance = "Erscheinungsbild", 16 chars, the longest tab label across the ten shipped locales; en "Appearance", ru "Оформление" are shorter) — plus unit pins in the existing tests/renderer/prefComponents/tabsBar.test.js, whose hoisted osState.isOsx mock already mounts BOTH style variants. (3) Visible keyboard focus (R-3): five interactive controls carry all: unset (or bare chrome) with no :focus-visible rule — verified absent by search: the settings toolbar .pref-tab (tabsBar/index.vue), the Quick Settings Aa button .quick-settings-btn (quickSettings/index.vue, whose existing :focus-visible rule covers only .quick-tab/.quick-openall), the View tab .quick-view-tab .theme-family-tile (viewTab.vue), the Page tab .quick-page-tab .linkish (pageTab.vue) and the sheet .pref-sheet-close (sheet/index.vue); each gains the C-SETTINGS-KEYBOARD-FOCUS canon rule — 2px solid var(--prefAccent) outline with 1px offset, :focus-visible only — beside the control's own chrome; selected/on/active state stays visually distinct from keyboard focus, pointer activation stays outline-free, and the already-covered switch/select/segment outlines keep passing unchanged. Evidence uses the real-keyboard checkKeyboardFocus harness canon (real Tab routes with the WebKit Option-Tab fallback recorded; a synthetic focus() call is insufficient), extended to the new targets in settings-shell.spec.ts (toolbar tab) and the new compact spec (Aa button, family tile, Reset row, open sheet's Close button). (4) Sheet focus trap (R-4): src/renderer/src/prefComponents/common/sheet/index.vue declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" but implements only a capture-phase window Escape handler (window.addEventListener('keydown', onKeydown, true) guarding on the open prop) — Tab walks out onto the dimmed page beneath, initial focus is not claimed and closing does not restore focus. The trap decision is RESOLVED AT PLAN TIME per the CAUTION: the pinned element-plus build (package.json "element-plus": "^2.14.8") ships the focus-trap component publicly — node_modules/element-plus/es/components/focus-trap/index.mjs exports ElFocusTrap (props loop/trapped/focusStartEl; the repo's established deep per-component import convention, main.js: import { ElDialog } from 'element-plus/es/components/dialog/index.mjs'; the el-dialog FocusTrap/@open-auto-focus precedent already rides in editor.vue's insert-table dialog) — so the sheet wires ElFocusTrap from element-plus/es/components/focus-trap/index.mjs with trapped bound to the open prop and loop enabled, gaining initial focus inside the panel, Tab/Shift+Tab cycling in both directions and automatic focus restore to the invoking control on release; the existing capture-phase Escape handler and its stopPropagation stay byte-identical, the 560px panel metrics and the three Advanced sheets' content flows (shortcutsSheet.vue, extensionsSheet.vue, customCssSheet.vue) are unchanged, and no new dependency is added; if the execution-time import check against the installed build ever fails, the same-semantics fallback is a hand-rolled Tab cycle inside the existing onKeydown capture handler (bounded replan, not a silent swap). Unit pins land in a new tests/renderer/pages/common/sheet.test.js per the pages/common canon; e2e trap integrity (no keystroke reaches the page behind while open; Escape and Close-button close both restore) rides the compact spec. (5) Aa Space activation (R-5): the Aa button binds @keydown.enter.prevent="toggle" only; it gains the components/recent/index.vue enter+space pair precedent (@keydown.enter.prevent="openRecentFile(file)" + @keydown.space.prevent="openRecentFile(file)" at recent/index.vue:103-104) as @keydown.space.prevent="toggle" with the default prevented, the Enter path unchanged — pinned red-first in the existing tests/renderer/components/quick-settings.test.js harness. Scope discipline: no window-size change (tauri.conf.json and mt_open_setting_window untouched), no palette/anatomy/interaction redesign, no i18n changes (every needed string exists, including preferences.advanced.sheets.close), no new dependencies/IPC/preference keys, no tabindex changes beyond what the sheet trap legitimately needs, no searchPanel/whats-new/workspace-dialog/unsaved-close work. CAUTION carried as a follow-up note, NOT an edit: the titlebar theme-toggle role="button" siblings (titleBar/index.vue .titlebar-nav-btn macOS and .frameless-titlebar-theme Win/Linux, both @keydown.enter.prevent-only and outline-less) stay OUT of this change's scope and are recorded in the bundle as the named follow-up. The F-id to surface mapping follows the spec assumption (F-002 Quick Settings fit, F-003 Settings navigation fit, F-005/F-006 visible focus, F-007 sheet trap, F-010 Aa Space) and is re-verified against the wave-35 findings report at execution start. Execution mode: T-001..T-005 strictly sequential (single-writer discipline; each task authors its own pins red-first against the pre-edit tree of that task, then turns them green); no grace-lint command appears inside this plan — lint runs only in the external target/final phases; GRACE semantic markup of every touched component (MODULE_CONTRACT, MODULE_MAP, CHANGE_SUMMARY, paired unique START_BLOCK_/END_BLOCK_ where new blocks are introduced) is synchronized per task, and the graph SummaryDeltas for M-061 (performance.xml) and M-011 (runtime.xml) plus the V-M-061/V-M-011 verification refs land in T-005 with the approved execution plan; applied bundles, frozen docs and the current graph/verification are not mutated while this spec is draft.

T-001.Title: M-061 Quick Settings viewport-bound layout: the panel height binding, pinned toolbar/footer, single-scroll body — approved mock metrics verbatim

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: author the compact geometry walker group in tests/e2e/compact-windows-fit.spec.ts (new file, viewport-pinned per the settings-shell.spec.ts canon — test.use 600x400, installTauriShim + bootEditor per the page-width-panel.spec.ts fixtures, open the panel via .quick-settings-btn per its openPanel helper) BEFORE editing the component: for each of the three tabs (page/view/tables) run the walker with the existing overflow tolerances and assert every .quick-settings-popover descendant rect lies fully inside the viewport below the title bar, the .quick-toolbar and the .quick-openall footer are visible and pinned (their rects constant while the body scrolls), the body scrolls when its content exceeds the remaining height and every row/control becomes reachable by that scroll alone, and nothing clips at the 600x400 minimum; run the focused group and record the pre-fix failures (footer clipped / panel past the viewport) in the bundle evidence. No successful skip, artificial sleep or disabled timing budget.

Implement ONLY the height binding in quickSettings/index.vue inside the existing START_BLOCK_QUICK_PANEL_METRICS block: the panel .quick-settings-popover gains max-height: calc(100vh - 64px) (the constant reserving the title-bar strip plus the 6px gap; macOS strip 30px per the tabsBar C-51 rule, Win/Linux frameless cells 46px — verified against both chrome forms), .quick-toolbar and .quick-openall gain flex-shrink: 0, and .quick-body loses max-height: 62vh, gaining flex: 1 1 auto and min-height: 0 with its existing overflow-y: auto and overflow-x: hidden kept — the body is the single scroll region and no other element scrolls. Every other rule in the block is byte-identical: position: absolute; top: calc(100% + 6px); right: 8px with the JS right-anchor in openPanel unchanged, width: 428px; max-width: calc(100vw - 32px);, border-radius: 12px;, the 0.5px border and the settings box-shadow, the palette blocks, the row anatomy block and the Aa glyph block untouched. At 640x620 and 1440x900 the cap must not bind below the natural content height, so the approved mock metrics and the current open/close semantics (window capture-phase mousedown closer, document Escape closer, bus entry) are unchanged. Open/close/toggle/openPanel/onDocMouseDown/onDocKeydown JavaScript byte-identical except semantic contract/change-summary comments; update MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY honestly (one new CHANGE_SUMMARY line, all pre-existing lines byte-identical, paired unique START_BLOCK_/END_BLOCK_ only if a new block is introduced).

Run the existing shell unit floor (tests/renderer/components/quick-settings.test.js green unchanged — open/close, outside click, Escape, bus entry, dark parity) and the renderer build, then re-run the focused compact walker group green. Review the walker output at all three tab states; if the required viewport fit cannot be reached within this scope (e.g. the 64px reserve is wrong on a real platform chrome), stop for a bounded scope revision — no relaxation of the walker tolerances and no per-platform constants beyond the one disclosed binding.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: extend the settings-shell.spec.ts overflow walker to the toolbar — the existing evaluate block gains .pref-toolbar and .pref-toolbar * alongside the .pref-body * set, asserting every element rect inside the viewport and toolbar/document scrollWidth at most innerWidth at the fixed 640x620 — and record the group failing (or the walker provably blind to the toolbar) on pre-fix code; author the tabsBar.test.js fit pins red-first in the existing per-OS describe: with the hoisted osState mock driving BOTH variants (isOsx true and false) the toolbar renders all seven .pref-tab buttons, the de stress catalog is asserted via the source-level readFileSync canon already used in that file (the sfc carries text-overflow: ellipsis and the stress labels come from static/locales/de.json — "Erscheinungsbild" named in the pin), and the mac variant's min-width: 76px floor plus the base min-width: 0 allowance are pinned in the sfc assertions; jsdom has no layout engine, so the geometric no-overflow proof lives in the e2e walker and the unit pins carry variant presence, routing, drag-region and CSS-shape assertions only.

Implement ONLY the shrink/ellipsis behavior in tabsBar/index.vue inside the existing START_BLOCK_TOOLBAR_METRICS block: the base .pref-toolbar .pref-tab gains min-width: 0 (shrink allowance), the mac variant keeps min-width: 76px (7x76px + 24px padding + gaps always fit the 640px window, so the approved floor never itself overflows), and .pref-tab-label gains overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis on BOTH variants (the shared label selector — a flex child, blockified, so ellipsis paints). Every other rule is byte-identical: both variant layouts, active-tab styling, paddings, the 28px traffic-light strip reservation, the border-bottom treatments, and the template/JavaScript (role="tablist", :data-tauri-drag-region="isOsx ? '' : null", aria-selected/aria-pressed, the search panel wiring) untouched — tab click and keyboard reachability unchanged. Update MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY honestly per the one-file convention.

Run the extended walker green in the settings-shell spec (mac variant, chromium — the underline variant is pinned at unit level via the osState mock; if the shim can seed a non-darwin window.electron.process.platform before app scripts load, the underline variant MAY additionally join the e2e, but it is not required), then the de-locale stress run: seed the prefs shim (the installFocusPreferences canon — mt_prefs_get_all override with language: 'de') and assert the toolbar reports no horizontal overflow and every .pref-tab rect stays inside the viewport with labels ellipsized, in both the light and dark parity runs the spec already drives. The macOS drag-region attribute, tab routing and the body's existing vertical scroll are pinned unchanged by the pre-existing spec groups staying green.

The compact spec runs --project=chromium per the spec's command; real keyboard input only — a synthetic focus() call is insufficient and never replaces reaching the target.

Implement ONLY the five focus-visible rules, each beside its control's own chrome in its owning file: quickSettings/index.vue gains .quick-settings-btn:focus-visible (the existing .quick-tab/.quick-openall rule untouched beside it), viewTab.vue gains .quick-view-tab .theme-family-tile:focus-visible, pageTab.vue gains .quick-page-tab .linkish:focus-visible, tabsBar/index.vue gains .pref-tab:focus-visible, sheet/index.vue gains the .pref-sheet-close:focus-visible rule — every one exactly outline: 2px solid var(--prefAccent); outline-offset: 1px; inside :focus-visible only, per the C-SETTINGS-KEYBOARD-FOCUS canon. No JavaScript focus manager, no tabindex changes, no new tokens or wrappers; selected/on/active state styling is untouched and stays visually distinct from the focus outline; pointer activation stays outline-free (pinned by the harness's pointer-first fresh context in the settings-shell canon). The existing switch/select/segment rules and their verification keep passing byte-identical.

Run the focus groups green in both engines the harness already drives where applicable (the compact spec per the spec's command is chromium; settings-shell keeps its chromium/webkit-settings projects), review the before/focused captures for ring clipping/overlap at all five targets (a 22px close button and 28px Aa button must not clip the 2px ring), and confirm Tab-away removes the outline. Existing component suites (bool/select/segmented/range, quick-settings shell) stay green unchanged.
